title: Physics Mock Test №6
subtitle: 45 tasks • 55 scored items • 3 hours • with formula sheet and calculator

questions.text: Using the given graph, find the acceleration of the body (m/s²). α = 58°, sin 58° = 0.85, cos 58° = 0.53.
A skier moving with an acceleration of 0.4 m/s² covered 100 m in 20 s. What are his speeds at the beginning and at the end of the path (m/s)?

A body thrown at an angle of 45° to the horizontal is still rising after 0.8 s, and the vertical component of its velocity is 12 m/s. Determine the distance between the launch point and the landing point of the body (m). g = 10 m/s².
A body thrown vertically upward returned to its initial position after 12 seconds. Find the maximum height reached by the body (m).
Two mutually perpendicular forces of 15 N and 20 N act on a body at rest with a mass of 2.5 kg. Find the speed of the body after 3 s (m/s).

The loads are suspended from pulleys as shown in the figure. If the masses of the loads are m₁ = 3 kg and m₂ = 6 kg, determine the acceleration of the load with the smaller mass (m/s²). Neglect friction and the masses of the pulleys.
By what factor is the weight of a body moving upward with an acceleration of 2 m/s² greater than its weight when moving downward with the same acceleration?

A puck of mass 150 g flying in the horizontal direction at a speed of 20 m/s hit the boundary at an angle of 60° to the normal to its surface and bounced off it. If the duration of the impact is 0.01 s, find the average force exerted by the puck on the boundary. Consider the collision perfectly elastic.
A bullet of mass m = 10 g moving at a speed of v = 100 m/s strikes inelastically a block attached to a spring. By how much does the spring compress (cm)? M = 1.99 kg, k = 200 N/m.

The density of one gas at a pressure of 400 kPa is 1.6 kg/m³. A second gas of mass 2 kg in a volume of 10 m³ has a pressure of 200 kPa. By what factor is the root-mean-square speed of the molecules of the second gas greater than that of the molecules of the first gas?

A cylinder with a capacity of 2 L is filled with helium at a pressure of 12·10⁵ Pa, and another cylinder with a volume of 5 L is filled with argon at a pressure of 2.2·10⁵ Pa. What pressure will be established if the cylinders are connected by a thin tube? The temperature is constant.
When 2 kg of oil was burned in an engine cylinder to heat the gas, the gas did 36 MJ of work. The specific heat of combustion of oil is 4.3·10⁷ J/kg. Determine the efficiency of the engine.
By how much does the internal energy of a monatomic ideal gas decrease if it is isobarically compressed at a pressure of 2·10⁵ Pa from a volume of 2.5 L to 1.6 L?

A vessel of volume 100 L contains air at a temperature of 25 °C and a relative humidity of 30 %. What will the relative humidity become if 1 g of water is introduced into the vessel? The density of saturated water vapor at 25 °C is 23 g/m³.
The same current flows through two copper conductors with diameters of 2 mm and 3 mm. By what factor is the drift speed of the electrons in the first conductor greater than in the second?

The primary winding of a step-down transformer with a transformation ratio of 8 is connected to a 220 V network. The resistance of the secondary winding is 2 Ω and the current in it is 3 A. Determine the voltage across the terminals of the secondary winding.

A parallel-plate air capacitor is connected to a DC voltage source. The energy of the capacitor is 5 μJ. What will the final energy of the capacitor be if the space between its plates is filled with kerosene with a dielectric constant of 2?

Two resistors, one with a resistance of 18 kΩ and the other with an unknown resistance, are connected in series to a 24 V DC source. If the voltage drop across the unknown resistance is 20 V, determine this resistance.
The amplitude values of the current and voltage across a resistor are 2.5 A and 120 V. Determine the power of the current.
When an external resistance of 6 Ω is connected to a current source, the current in the circuit is 0.3 A, and with an external resistance of 14 Ω it is 0.15 A. Determine the short-circuit current.
By what factor does the inductive reactance of a coil decrease if it is disconnected from an AC circuit with a frequency of 10 kHz and connected to a circuit with a current frequency of 50 Hz?
What is the inductance of a coil (H) if, at a current of 2.5 A, a flux linkage of 25 Wb arises in it?
The Lorentz force acting on a charge of 0.4 C moving at a speed of 1 km/s perpendicular to the induction lines is 8 N. What is the magnetic induction (mT)?
A steady electric current of 3 A flows through a coil with an inductance of 4 H. What is the energy of the magnetic field of the coil (J)?

The capacitance of the capacitor in an ideal oscillating circuit is 4 μF, and the charge on it varies according to the law q = 2·10⁻⁵ cos(10⁵πt) (C). Find the maximum value of the magnetic field energy in the circuit.

A circuit is made up of an inductor and 3 identical capacitors connected in series. The oscillation period of the circuit is 10 μs. What will the oscillation period of the circuit be if the capacitors are connected in parallel?
An object is located 25 cm in front of the focus of a converging lens. The image is formed 35 cm beyond the double focal point. Determine the focal length of the lens.
If the magnification of a lens is 4 when the distance from the object to the lens is 15 cm, find the focal length of the lens (cm).
If the longest wavelength of light capable of causing the photoelectric effect in cesium is 620 nm, find the work function of an electron from cesium (eV).

If the maximum speed of photoelectrons emitted from cadmium, for which the electron work function is 6.56·10⁻¹⁹ J, is 4·10⁵ m/s, find the wavelength of the radiation incident on the cadmium. c = 3·10⁸ m/s, h = 6.625·10⁻³⁴ J·s, mₑ = 9.1·10⁻³¹ kg.
If, when an electron in a hydrogen atom moves from a higher stationary orbit to a lower one, its energy decreases by 1.8 eV, find the wavelength of the radiation. c = 3·10⁸ m/s, h = 6.625·10⁻³⁴ J·s.
Identify the missing particle in this nuclear reaction: ⁷₃Li + ? → ¹⁰₅B + ¹₀n.
If the temperature of the gas in the first state is known to be 150 K, determine the temperature in the next state (K).
